newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. will not negotiate presence in Panama.
newsitem.headline: U.S. will not negotiate presence in Panama.

text.p: The United States will not enter into exploratory talks with Panama to discuss a military presence in the next century, U.S. Embassy spokesman Joe Johnson told Reuters on Sunday.
"The issue of U.S. bases per se is off the table. But U.S. participation in a proposal for an anti-drug centre at Howard Air Force Base (in Panama) is on the table," Johnson said.

The decision came a week after President Ernesto Perez Balladares surprised U.S. and Panamanian officials by announcing, at a ruling party youth rally, that Panama would not enter into talks with the United States to negotiate a military presence in Panama in the next century.
Perez Balladares said Panama would enter the 21st century without the presence of foreign military installations.

Johnson said the president's decision did not affect possible talks on converting strategic Howard Air Force Base into an international drug interdiction centre. Perez Balladares had said the United States could keep Howard in Panama at no cost for such a purpose.
John Negroponte, the U.S. coordinator of the Panama bases talks, was planning a trip to Panama before the end of the year, Johnson said.
"I think Negroponte and Washington can well address that issue of a proposal for an anti-drug centre at Howard," he said.
